summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (Lahdo Traitor 1/66)

data.turoyo: ḥa mənne mʕanatle hawxa aʕmi, qḥir.
data.translation: one of them was displeased with me. He was furious!

rationale: Thin Preterit cell: explicit experiencer and ʕal target rather than only a bare paradigm form.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (MAC NE Interview 2/239)

data.turoyo: ḥəngi aṭ+ṭaye mʕantiwa minan, əmmi d ... aq+qoruǧiye mʕantiwa minan, əmmi, ‘Dhowe qaṭlo ba+d̥koṯani, gəzzoxu eba!
data.translation: Because the Muslims hated us so much, they say that… the village guards hated us so much, they say, ‘If there is any killing in these places, you will be in the thick of it (lit. ‘you will go into it’)’.

rationale: Thin Infectum-wa cell: repeated plural experiencers and m-target, with edition's hatred wording retained.

data.turoyo: Komər i emo ġalabe mʕanatla w aṯi eba zaḥme.
data.translation: Da wurde die Mutter sehr zornig und es kam ihr sehr hart an.

rationale: Thin Preterit cell: feminine experiencer with -la and no overt target.

data.turoyo: <...> Saləq hano Tawfig Be d kumarnox, d kəmʕanət mənayna. <...>
data.translation: <...> This Tawfiq Bey, whom I tell you about, who was angry with us, went upstairs. <...>

rationale: Fills the Infectum cell, still at one after round 1; overt named experiencer and mənayna target support the already clarified m-government. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation.

data.translation: <...> He too was angry with him... <...>

rationale: Fills the Infectum-wa cell, at two including round 1; compact state clause with mene target. Pronoun identities are left as in the source rather than reconstructed. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation.

data.turoyo: Bu ʕantano d komʕantutu m ḥḏoḏe, ma mən kəbʕitu m ḥḏoḏe? Mən kətxu qəm ḥḏoḏe? <...>
data.translation: With the hostility that you bear one another, what do you want from one another? What do you have against one another? <...>

rationale: Fills the thin Infectum cell and supplies 2pl komʕantutu with an overt reciprocal m ḥḏoḏe target; reciprocal meaning does not require Detransitive morphology. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation.
Lahdo Traitor 1/66 supplies aʕmi as target; MAC NE Interview 2/239 and inherited 85/5 supply minan/me-Midən. This clarifies the target government, not a separate hatred sense.

summary: Experiencer coding is active-shaped: masculine mʕanatle and feminine mʕanatla use the l-set despite emotional intransitive semantics. These are not Detransitive forms.
Targets alternate ʕal (aʕmi) and m- (minan; me-Midən). A place name in the inherited example stands for its inhabitants.
Infectum-wa describes sustained past hostility and habitual attitudes; Preterit foregrounds becoming angry. The English 'hated us' does not by itself establish a separate hatred sense.
The reconstructed Samson fragment is retained only as uncertain evidence; no complete suffix or overt target can be inferred from the interrupted relative clause.

Experiencer subjects occur with kəmʕanət, komʕantutu and past-state mʕanatwo. The anger target is mənayna, mene or m ḥḏoḏe; the latter is reciprocal in the argument phrase, without Detransitive marking.
Jan 2.4/570 has Infectum in a narrative relative clause; past narrative reference in the supplied English does not make it Preterit. Jan 2.4/582 has overt -wo and belongs to Infectum-wa.
The cognate nominal frame bu ʕantano d komʕantutu in Jan 3.56/1679 emphasizes hostility; the Turoyo does not require a separately numbered hatred sense or a light-verb idiom.
Confirm the restored dәmʕan<atte> at MAC NE Samson the hero/20 and its box; the supplied ending is not a fully heard form.
Do ʕal and m- target coding differ in meaning or distribution, or are they dialect alternatives?
Confirm the PrS 36/122 versus inherited prs 97/19 concordance before changing references.
Does the written 2pl komʕantutu reflect a regular local variant alongside the singular mʕanət? Retain the attested spelling and compare dialectal forms before changing the base forms.
All three Jan occurrences support the round-1 clarification of m- target government; the reciprocal target m ḥḏoḏe retains active II morphology. No further gloss change is proposed.
